headline: Riyadh Airport Reopening Now Depends on Air Defence
deck: Saudi Arabia reopened Riyadh terminals after more than two weeks as it reported intercepting Houthi weapons; the next threat will test whether passengers can keep moving.
body: Saudi Arabia reopened its main airport for international flights more than two weeks after strikes put it out of service, and said earlier Sunday that it intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile and drone. King Khalid International Airport said terminals 1 and 2 were open for domestic and international flights from Sunday. [E1][E2]
Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki, the Saudi military spokesman, said the intercepted ballistic missile and drone had been fired by the Houthis early Sunday. [E3]

The Houthis said they had carried out seven operations using ballistic missiles and drones against Saudi airports, oil facilities and an air base in retaliation for Saudi airstrikes in Yemen; they said King Khalid International Airport was among their targets. [E4][E5]

**The desk's reading.** The reopening and the interception are one operating problem: passenger access now relies on air defences stopping threats before they interrupt terminal operations. The strongest competing reading is that the reported interception shows the defences can permit a durable return to service. But the same day’s claims of operations against the airport make the reopening a test of continuity rather than a completed restoration.

**The next test.** When the Houthis next declare a threat against King Khalid International Airport, the observable split is whether the airport keeps its reopened terminals in passenger service or suspends them again; continued service would support the view that interception can sustain access, while a suspension would overturn it.
